name: Fleshrender
body:
Fleshrender CR 3

XP 800
CE Medium undead
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 12, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 36 (5d8+12)
Fort +2, Ref +3, Will +5
Defensive Abilities channel resistance +6

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +4 (1d8+2)
Special Attacks consume flesh

STATISTICS

Str 15; Dex 15, Con —; Int 13; Wis 14; Cha 14
Base Atk +2; CMB +3; CMD 15
Feats Weapon Finesse, Improved Grapple, Improved Unarmed Strike
Skills Acrobatics +4, Climb +6, Perception +7, Stealth +7
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Consume Flesh (Su)

A fleshrender can consume flesh from a grappled opponent. If the fleshrender successfully grapples an opponent and deals subsequent physical damage, the flreshrender heals 4 hit points or gains 4 temporary hit points for 1 hour (up to a maximum number of temporary hit points equal to its full normal hit points).

ECOLOGY

Environment any land
Organization solitary, group (2–4), party (5-20)
Treasure standard

The dreadful fleshrender is an undead entity known for cannibalism. When a humanoid has consumed another sentient being’s flesh, there is a chance that the cannibal will return as a fleshrender after death. In rare and heinous circumstances, entire remote villages or wilderness parties become fleshrenders during a hard winter or famine.

Fleshrenders attack by grappling their opponents and then consuming them. Fleshrenders, while intelligent, are driven by insatiable hunger, and negotiating with a fleshrender is almost unheard of. Fleshrenders will often harass their prey with yelling and taunts while attacking, as fleshrenders both speak Common and are highly malicious.

Fleshrenders may appear as any sentient humanoid race, and may be male or female. They appear as darkened versions of their former self, with pale, shriveled features and red, glowing eyes. They are accompanied by a faint red mist. This mist grows thicker as the number of fleshrenders encountered increases.
